name: professor
description: Professor's assistant inside VS Code: opens the pfm chat fleet in terminals that carry each chat's live name and land you where you asked, paints the terminal, and every window's title, activity and status bars and borders (local and Remote-SSH), in Claude Code's theme, which `pfm theme` renders; and lists every pfm theme in VS Code's Color Theme picker as Professor · {name}, where picking one switches every surface to it; and an Analyze link above line 1 of a prompt file that has Claude check it against Professor's prompt law through pfm, its errors, warnings and info in the Problems panel with a quick fix for each rewrite.

professor.terminal.env.description: Environment for a Professor terminal; PFM_AUTO_OPEN opens the pfm picker once the shell is up.

professor.terminal.icons.description: Codicons a new Professor terminal cycles through, so each tab reads apart at a glance.

professor.terminal.colors.description: Theme colours cycled beside the icons on the same counter, so a pair repeats only every least-common-multiple of the two list lengths.

professor.theme.stateDir.description: Directory pfm theme writes its contract (current.json) to; empty means ~/.local/state/pfm/theme. The terminal follows Claude Code's theme only after pfm theme on.

professor.promptLint.globs.description: Glob patterns of the prompt files that show the Analyze link.

professor.promptLint.model.description: Claude model the Analyze run uses (pfm headless exec --model).

professor.promptLint.effort.description: Reasoning effort the Analyze run uses (pfm headless exec --effort).

professor.promptLint.timeout.description: Seconds an Analyze run may take before pfm stops it (pfm headless exec --timeout).
